html:
A skyscraper in Taipei, Taiwan, 508 metres tall with 101 floors above ground, opened at the end of 2004. It was the tallest building in the world until the Burj Khalifa in Dubai passed it in 2010.

It took the title from the Petronas Towers in Kuala Lumpur. The design, by the firm of C. Y. Lee, stacks eight sections like a bamboo stalk or a pagoda, with eight a lucky number in Chinese tradition.

Taipei sits in a zone of earthquakes and typhoons, so the tower has a huge steel ball, a tuned mass damper of over 600 tonnes, hung near the top to steady it in the wind. Its New Year fireworks are broadcast around the world.

The tower stands for the wealth Taiwan built from electronics and trade after the 1980s, and for its wish to be seen on the world stage.
